subject: Defining MAP success criteria, exit gates & acceptance tests
thread_messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emily Pruitt <e.pruitt@novamed.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Defining MAP success criteria, exit gates & acceptance tests

Hi Emily (and team),

Attached is a first-pass mutual action plan (MAP) and an initial acceptance-test catalog for the 4-week evaluation you asked for. High-level asks: please review the success criteria below and flag anything that won't work for Novamed.

Proposed evaluation scope and exit gates (top-level):
- Functionality: end-to-end embedding + reranking pipeline working with Novamed sample dataset (see sample-dataset-brief.csv).
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency <= 450ms for 2k token batches under test workload.
- Throughput: sustain 120 requests/min steady-state with <2% error rate.
- Quality: precision@5 on reranker >= 0.78 vs. Novamed gold set (we included baseline scripts).
- Security/compliance: SOC2 controls evidence and encrypted-in-transit/storage proof; no PII persists beyond session.
- Integration: API keys and webhook delivery tested with your staging environment (sandbox.redwood.com).

Acceptance-test examples (see acceptance-tests.csv): smoke run, sample-queries concordance, latency sweep, failure/retry scenarios, load ramp and KV cache warm-up measurement.

Timeline (draft):
- Week 0 (this week): kickoff, MAP sign-off, procurement triage
- Week 1: integration & smoke tests (basic connectivity + sample queries)
- Week 2: performance runs + quality baseline comparisons
- Week 3: edge-case tests, security checklist, canary and access handoff
- Week 4: signoff or rollback decision; finalize SLA language

Please annotate the attached MAP (MAP-draft-v1.pdf) with questions and return by Thursday EOD PT so we can finalize scope with procurement. If the latency/throughput targets need adjustment based on your production profile, tell us which metrics drive the business impact and we’ll adapt.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Defining MAP success criteria, exit gates & acceptance tests

Marissa — thanks for the clear draft. A few quick notes from our side after a quick read:

Inline:
- Latency: 450ms P95 looks aggressive for our current routing (requests hit multiple services); can we provide a staged target: P95 <= 650ms in week 2, aim for <=450ms by week 4 if infra tuning is required?
- Quality: we’ll run the provided baseline but we need a reproducible test harness; can you include the exact seed/test fixtures you’ll use?
- Security: procurement asked for a SOC2 summary + certificate and a brief on data retention policies. I’m CCing procurement now.
- Acceptance tests: add a test for redaction/PII handling in outputs (critical for us).

Procurement contact: Novamed Procurement <procurement@novamed.com> — they will own contracts and minimal security evidence.

We can try to return annotated MAP by Friday COB if you can confirm the staged latency targets and share the test harness. Also: can Ben share a short list of the sample queries you need from us (we’ll pull a 500-row validation set).

—Emily

-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emily Pruitt <e.pruitt@novamed.com>, Novamed Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Defining MAP success criteria, exit gates & acceptance tests

Thanks Emily — good feedback. Quick responses and owners below; annotating the plan now.

- Latency (owner: Ben Carter): we can commit to a staged SLA in the MAP: P95 <= 650ms during baseline runs (week 2) and a stretch goal of <=450ms by week 4 with infra tuning and KV warm-up. Ben — can you confirm the profiling steps and expected warm-up duration?
- Test harness & fixtures (owner: Karthik Iyer): we’ll publish the harness (pytest + reproducible seed) and the script to load your 500-row validation set. Karthik, target to post to the shared doc by Wednesday noon.
- PII/redaction test (owner: Hannah Schmitt): Hannah will add a redaction verification test to acceptance-tests.csv and a short runbook for reviewers. Hannah, please include expected result format (masked tokens + audit log entries).
- Security evidence (owner: Marissa + Legal): I’ll pull the SOC2 summary and a short data-retention statement into the MAP. Procurement — welcome. I’ll loop in Legal once procurement lists required artifacts.

Updated timeline:
- Thu (7/31): annotated MAP back to Novamed; we’ll include staged latency wording, test harness link, and redaction test.
- Wed (8/6): internal demo & full performance run with your sample dataset
- Thu (8/14): joint review & decision checkpoint (signoff, request changes, or stop)

Related links: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Gz-MapDraft (working MAP) — I’ll add owners inline. HubSpot: 1254882 is the deal record.

Action items for Novamed:
- Provide 500-row validation set (Ben will send a template)
- Confirm procurement artifacts required (SOC2 + any additional checklists)

Marissa
